articleTitle: The Role of Nuclear Micro Reactors to Reach Net-Zero by 2050
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: This paper provides brief information on the current nuclear power plant types, and the scope of development to set carbon-free emissions by 2050. This research will help to identify new studies, designs, and developments of small modular nuclear reactors and share available knowledge on the recent development of nuclear reactors. It will help to address the consistency of renewable energy and provide high-base electricity to nullify the renewable energy issues. Small modular nuclear reactors specifically micro reactors design will become a power pack of energy production within the limited space required to provide consistent electricity to all. The paper includes brief information about the countries agreeing to reduce their carbon footprint from the earth to reach net zero by 2050 with the help of available nuclear technologies. Eeio Solutions promises to share in-depth knowledge of its Nuclear Micro Reactor design and development. The company addresses global climate change issues and encourages the development of nuclear technological energy products. Available renewable energy sources provide electricity with conditions, but only nuclear reactor technology promises high-base carbon-free electricity generation. The company is in its first research phase to make its first Nuclear Micro Reactor design to reach a global mission of net zero carbon emission by 2050. This would be a great initiative that can help to reduce climate change and provide electricity to remote locations.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Implementation for Energy Optimization and Fraud Detection in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: The evaluative aspect of smart grid (SG) is energy fraud detection for two-way network privacy and security conservation. Energy Optimization is a critical situation in SG, especially when large number of consumers and prosumers are integrated within the system. Data mining and machine learning (ML) have been widely used to recognize patterns of normal and abnormal behavior and for intelligent analysis of SG. In this research paper a novel technique of machine learning (ML) is used to detect energy fraud and demand side management (DSM) by analyzing energy consumption reports by implementing a deep neural network (DNN) based algorithm over a pre-determined interval of time. The main advantage of the proposed technique is to recognize unauthorized energy user's activities especially for those customers who use renewable energy sources (RES) and grid energy for infrequent intervals of time. By detecting energy fraud, the efficiency of the entire system is enhanced by saving energy and its utilization for valuable purposes, which is beneficial both for suppliers and consumers.

Author Keywords: Artificial and Deep Neural Network (ANN & DNN)

articleTitle: Phase-Shift Variable-Frequency Control Strategy of a Single-Stage Micro Inverter Based on Dual Active Bridge Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: This paper investigates the operation principle and the control method for a single-stage micro inverter based on the dual active bridge topology. The mathematical model of the inverter is rigorously derived for the design of the controller. The inverter is controlled by a single phase shift modulation method in which the switching frequency varies with the phase shift angle so that the output current is linear to the phase shift angle. Consequently, the parameters of the feed-back PI controller is easy to design. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed phase-shift variable frequency control strategy. The THD of the grid current is less than 2.6%, and soft-switching can be realized in a wide range except the region near the zero crossing point of the grid voltage.

articleTitle: Improvement of Microgrids Operation Considering Demand Response Using Imperialist Competitive Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: In recent years, with the restructuring and privatization of power networks, special attention has been paid to the role of customers in network operation. Therefore, demand response programs have played an important role in power network studies and many researchers have been working in this area. Microgrids are a collection of loads and generating units that can supply their own power independently. In this article, the problem of demand response of loads in a microgrid has been studied. For this purpose, the customers in a microgrid announce their proposed prices for participating in the demand response program to the network operator for different hours of the day. This demand response program will be executed when the network operation constraints are violated. Therefore, there is no need to run it in the hours when the network is operating properly. The network operator will run the demand response program with the aim of removing the constraints imposed on the network. For this purpose, the imperialist competitive algorithm (lCA) has been used to find the best possible solution. After running the proposed method, it will be determined how much power each load should reduce in each hour. The proposed method has been implemented on a sample network and its results have been evaluated and analyzed for different scenarios. The problem modeling has been done using MATLAB software. The results proved the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Utilizing Packet Tracer Simulation to Modern Smart Campus Initiatives for a Sustainable Future
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: This study presents an integrated network of a smart campus design for a Sultanate of Oman higher education institution. The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of networked devices that can gather and send data without the intervention of humans. IoT is employed in many different fields these days, such as industry, agriculture, medicine, smart cities, etc. This paper discusses smart campuses, which include smart gardens that sprinkle water based on water levels, smart classrooms that monitor temperature in response to surroundings, and smart grids that use solar energy to transfer electricity to power meters that help light bulbs and charge batteries. To provide top-notch resources to teachers, staff, and students on campus, smart campuses are contemporary urban concepts. The global perception of smart campuses is still limited despite the high-tech, rational, and controllable obstacles. The primary aim of this study is to present a novel idea known as the “Modern Smart Campus.” This will streamline operations and contribute to a sustainable future. Cisco Packet Tracer 8.2 simulates the relevant work in this article.

articleTitle: Power Quality Analytical Methodology Using Signal Processing and Machine Learning Techniques for Grid Fault Classification and Location Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: The increase in global energy demand with a growing dynamic power system has made today's electrical network a complex infrastructure where increased faults and grid violations are being reported at higher rates. Also, with an increased penetration of intermittent Distributed Energy Resource (DER), the detection of transient events occurring in a large network is becoming challenging and therefore encouraging potential areas of research in this field. Furthermore, the deployment of high-resolution devices such as PMU gives access to vast amounts of data and carries vital information to ensure grid safety and protection. This paper analyzes a methodology to detect and predict power system disturbances and fault location in electrical power network (distribution & transmission) using data-driven & machine learning techniques. It uses signal processing techniques based on multi-level discrete wavelet transforms, with wavelet spectral energy/entropy-based feature extraction stage to train ANN (Artificial Neural Network) classifiers to predict and classify faults in power system applications. Machine learning classification techniques are used based on a dataset which is generated with single measurement point in simulation environment where grid model is used with varying fault conditions such as alternating phase & neutral impedance, inception angle & distance. A comparative analysis is performed with ANN and other potential classifiers to identify potential limitation & improvements in feature extraction stage to better classify faults and location. Furthermore, PQ events such as voltage sag, voltage swell, and transient event have been analyzed and the propagating effect of faults in the network, medium voltage to low voltage network are also discussed.

articleTitle: Full Load Range Efficiency Optimisation Control of the Phase-Shifted Full-Bridge Series Resonant Converter in a Two-Stage PV Micro Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: This paper presents the mathematical model and control system of a phase shift full bridge series resonant con-verter serving as the first stage of a two-stage PV micro inverter, where the converter operates in very wide input voltage range and full load range. The function of output power versus control signals, hardware parameters and measured signals is rigorously derived. The proposed control system applies three degrees of freedom, including duty cycle, switching frequency, and phase shift angle, to ensure full load range efficiency optimisation. The zero voltage switching capability in heavy load conditions and the frequency limiting characteristics in light load conditions are both verified in simulation results. The results of the experiment show that the peak efficiency is up to 97.7% when the input voltage is 30V, while the light load efficiency (10% of the power rating) is still higher than 90 % even when the input voltage increases to 55v.

articleTitle: A Multi-Sensory Cattle Monitoring System With Wireless and Solar Charging Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Livestock plays a vital role in socioeconomic growth, and it is necessary to improve the quantity and quality of animal products. The precision livestock farming paradigm aims to increase food production while maintaining animal welfare using sensors, the Internet of Things (IoT), and predictive analytics. This research proposes a cattle monitoring system that features an accelerometer for activity detection, a photoplethysmography sensor for heart rate and oxygen saturation, a thermistor, and a GPS module. An ESP32-based board with integrated Wi-Fi collects and sends data to a server. Additionally, the proposed system is equipped with solar and wireless charging capabilities, eliminating the need for manual charging or battery replacement. The wireless charging system consists of three receiving coils located in the cattle monitoring system and two receiving coils in the cattle feeding and resting area. Finally, the total energy consumption of all electronic components was 22.6Wh, while the combined energy produced by the solar panels and wireless charging system was 36.7Wh, thus satisfying the energy requirements of the device.

articleTitle: Quadratic-Equation Based Volt-Watt Control Rules Design Strategy to Mitigate Overvoltage in Power Grids with High Penetration of Solar Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: The over-voltage issue caused by the high penetration of non-controllable PV generators is a significant challenge for power grids, particularly in distribution networks. Various international standards recommend volt-watt curves to address over-voltage issues, but determining set points on those curves is typically left to grid designers. This paper aims to design control rules with a decentralized approach, allowing each PV unit to locally decide its active power curtailment level without involving a central controller for real-time data exchange. The proposed approach uses the sensitivity values of PV inverters to create a quadratic equation curve, ensuring a more equitable contribution of PV inverters in active power curtailment (APC). This method ensures that all PV inverters enter the shut-down mode concurrently, promoting fairness in shut-down scenarios. The IEEE 37 Bus system was selected to evaluate the proposed approach, yielding positive results. The proposed method is straightforward to implement and effective in facilitating fair APC. The results demonstrate more than 30% improvement during peak PV generation times.

articleTitle: Model-Based Reactive Power Control for Grid-Tied Micro-Inverter in Discontinuous Current Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: For the reduction of turn-on loss during reactive power control of discontinuous current mode (DCM) grid-tied micro-inverter, this paper divides the working process of the micro-inverter into inverter mode and rectifier mode over a grid period based on the polarities of reference current and grid voltage. According to the time intervals in one switching cycle of different modes, the operation principles are analyzed, and the precise time domain expressions of the inductor current and drain-to-source voltage are calculated in each time interval. Then, accurate average inductor current models are proposed respectively to achieve zero voltage switching (ZVS) in inverter mode and valley switching (VS) in rectifier mode, which can significantly reduce the turn-on loss. The effectiveness of the proposed method was verified by simulation and experiments using a 1000W laboratory prototype.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wind Power Forecasting Accuracy in Canada Using a Solar Data-Enhanced Hybrid Machine Learning Model: Integrating ANN, LSTM, and SVR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: As the world moves toward sustainable energy solutions, wind power emerges as a pivotal renewable energy (RE) source due to its accessibility and zero carbon emission. However, its unpredictable nature poses significant forecasting challenges, that impact energy management efficiency. This study tackles this vital challenge by integrating solar power data into advanced machine learning models to enhance the forecast accuracy and quantifying uncertainty of wind power. The MERRA-2 dataset – a comprehensive atmospheric reanalysis from NASA – spanning 2017 to 2019 across three locations of Canadian provinces, British Colombia, Manitoba, and Nova Scotia has been considered for this work. A novel hybrid machine learning framework that combines the strengths of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTM), and Support Vector Machines (SVM), has been used. Utilizing this framework excels in pattern recognition, temporal data processing, and regression analysis, effectively will improve the precision of wind power forecasts. Besides, it provides a robust framework for quantifying forecast uncertainty and enhancing decision-making in renewable energy management. The superiority of this model is demonstrated through comparative evaluations against conventional methods using various metrics to establish its efficacy and applicability in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Carbon Emission Accounting and Prediction Method for Industrial Parks Considering Integrated Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Industrial parks are key to achieving carbon neutrality goals due to their significant contributions to China's economy and carbon emissions. However, standardized carbon emission accounting systems for these parks are lacking. This study presents a multi-layered carbon emission accounting model for industrial parks, incorporating energy supply, consumption, and non-energy sectors. An empirical analysis of a Wuxi industrial park's carbon emissions from 2015 to 2022 was conducted. Using the LEAP model, three scenarios (baseline, emission reduction, and enhanced emission reduction) were constructed to project the park's energy demand and carbon emissions from 2020 to 2060. Results show a 68.97% reduction in carbon emissions compared to 2020 under the enhanced scenario, and a 41.67% reduction compared to the baseline. Based on this, the study proposes the following carbon reduction pathways: increasing the installed capacity of renewable energy generation on the supply side and enhancing the electrification rate of end-use sectors on the consumption side.

articleTitle: An Optimized Shade-Tolerant MPPT for Photovoltaic Systems Using AI-Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Multiple artificial intelligence (AI) regression and metaheuristic search techniques have been proposed for Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) of Photovoltaic (PV) systems. However, their reliability under Partial Shading (PS) is still questionable given that it occurs at various depths, shapes, and surface areas. This work presents a robust Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) technique for Photovoltaic (PV) systems under Partial Shading (PS). Motivated by the ON/OFF nature of the bypass diodes, the infinite PS patterns are grouped into distinct discretized regions each containing a single MPP. An artificial neural classifier is trained to identify the region of the Global MPP (GMPP). Once the GMPP class is obtained, a Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) is launched to locate it. Additionally, a class zero is assigned to account for the overlapping of the regions due to the expansion and contraction of the I-V curve for extreme temperature and irradiance conditions. The superiority of the proposed method is verified experimentally.

articleTitle: Active LiFePO4 Battery Cell Balancing Based on a Flyback Converter for Battery Storage Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4) rechargeable batteries are widely used by electric utility companies in battery storage applications. Battery cells are combined to form a battery module. Each module is constantly monitored with sensors and controlled by a Battery Management System (BMS). The BMS performs balancing of the cells. Each cell in the battery stack is monitored to maintain a healthy battery state of charge (SoC). The motivation for this work is to develop an active balancing system to replace a passive system currently being performed manually on an existing battery storage system. An active cell balancer was designed using the LT8584 active cell balancer. An LTspice simulation was created for a single cell. It demonstrates critical parameters of the flyback converter cycle time. A PCB board, designed using KiCAD, is presented. Building and testing of this board is in progress. It is anticipated that the proposed design could be used to restore the health of SoC of faulty modules in lieu of removing and replacing them with a new module, resulting in potential cost savings. The proposed design is scalable in that it could be used for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> number of cells in a battery module consisting of LiFePO4 battery cells.

articleTitle: ANN-Based Voltage Stability Assessment with PMU Infrastructure Placement Consideration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Artificial intelligence has led to increasingly significant technological advancements in a variety of sectors, including electrical power systems. The traditional methods to assess the stability of electric power systems typically need a significant amount of processing time and a complete set of network parameters. Many data points will be generated due to the high resolution of the Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) measurement results. As a result, an efficient and effective way to process this data is required. The objective of this study is to establish a voltage stability detection method utilizing the artificial neural network approach by assessing its performance based on metrics. In addition, the costs associated with PMU and communication infrastructure will be assessed for each scenario. The imbalance in data distribution between classes and the location of PMU used in the dataset affects the performance of the detection. This research indicates that selecting an unsuitable PMU location can lead to poor performance in voltage stability assessment below 80%. Furthermore, the choice of metrics should align with the characteristics and objectives of the analysis. It is also important to consider the cost variables to minimize the costs related to PMU installation while still ensuring the reliability of detection performance.

articleTitle: Design of a Water Quality Monitoring System Powered By a Savonius Hydrokinetic Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Water quality monitoring is essential due to the constant variation in its properties caused by pollutants, environmental changes, or other factors. This paper proposes the design of a real-time water quality monitoring system powered by a Savonius turbine. The VDI 2221 guideline is used for the design process. The proposed system measures temperature, electrical conductivity (EC), pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), total dissolved solids (TDS), turbidity, and pressure. The total energy consumption of all components is 32.92Wh. The Savonius turbine was analyzed using two-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD). It was found that at a water velocity of 1.02m/s, the turbine, under load conditions, torque coefficient of 0.28, and power coefficient of 0.322, the alternator reached 150RPM. Under these conditions, the alternator provides 100Wh, satisfying the energy consumption of the system.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Concept for Output Current Prediction of MPPT P&O Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: This paper investigates the prediction of photovoltaic controller output current based on the digital twin concept. A solar emulator is used as the physical system of a real solar power plant to predict the future electricity output of a solar photovoltaic system. Using both the characteristics of the photovoltaic panel and the weather conditions specific to the location of the physical system, irradiation data varying between 500 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>and 1500 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>are used to predict the current with new sunshine value. Prediction of the output current based on data from the physical twin is a novel contribution not found in previous studies. A linear regression type machine learning algorithm was used to train the current data taken by the data acquisition system. Simulation results indicate that the prediction method is effective with a root mean square error (RMSE) close to 1. Evaluation of the MPPT P&O algorithm and the prediction algorithm demonstrates the effectiveness of linear regression for solar PV controller output current prediction.

articleTitle: Enhancing Transient Stability in an Islanded Microgrid Including Electric Vehicles Using SMES
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Energy storage resources such as flywheels, ultracapacitors, and superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) are commonly used to improve the transient stability of power systems. Compared to flywheels and ultracapacitors, SMES exhibits lower standby losses and higher efficiency, making it more suitable for long-term operations. This paper focuses on controlling SMES to enhance the transient stability of electric vehicle (EV) charging stations within a microgrid. A control method for SMES is proposed to effectively manage transient conditions in the microgrid, including fault occurrences, disconnection of a large generation unit, and the addition of a large load (such as an EV charging station). The performance of the proposed SMES control system is evaluated through MATLAB simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving the transient stability of the EV charging stations within the microgrid. The key contribution of this work is the evaluation of the impact of a SMES control system on enhancing the transient stability of microgrids with EV charging stations. The results show that the proposed SMES control system can effectively mitigate the transient instability issues caused by the intermittent renewable sources and dynamic EV loads, ensuring reliable and stable operation of the microgrid.

articleTitle: Profit-Oriented Electricity Price Forecast Method for Demand Responses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel electricity price forecast method for demand responses (DRs) who participate in the electricity market. The conventional forecast methods, especially machine learning-based methods, tend to model the featured training data by minimizing the mean-square-error (MSE). In such methods, the loss function is defined to be the MSE. However, due to the characteristics of the DRs, a forecast result with a good MSE value is not necessarily more beneficial for the DRs in a deregulated market environment. Alternatively, the proposed method modifies the conventional loss function to inclusively consider the gradient of the forecast data. The loss function is designed in such a way as to improve the Extremum Timing Accuracy (ETA), a profit-oriented criterion of the forecast results so that the economic benefits of the DRs can be further boosted. Forecast results on the clearing price of the day-ahead energy wholesale market in Japan, the JEPX spot market, by neural network with the proposed profit-oriented loss function are tested. Performance comparison with the conventional neural network forecast is also reported. It is proved that the proposed forecast method increases the market profit of the DR successfully.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Flux Switching Permanent Magnet Machine Using Segmented Rotor with Multi-Layer Flux Barriers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Many topologies of flux switching permanent magnet machines have been developed in recent years as they gained higher attraction due to high torque and power densities. The transverse laminated rotor flux switching permanent magnet machine utilizes multilayer flux barriers added to a segmented rotor flux switching permanent magnet machine with the aim of increasing the electromagnetic performance. Although the results showed a 3.5N m torque enhancement and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> efficiency improvement, it could have improved more with more detailed optimization of flux barriers. Therefore, this paper focuses on the positioning of the flux barriers through an optimization analysis using a fractional factorial experiment method. The influence of the geometrical parameters on the performance of this machine is investigated by FEA analysis and then optimized with different objectives. The output torque maximization goal leads to 0.65Nm of torque enhancement and almost 0.5% increase in the efficiency.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Medium-Term Load Forecasting in Smart Commercial Building
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Accurate forecasting of electrical loads is a significant part of monitoring and managing building efficiency to optimize energy consumption, reduce costs, and improve overall sustainability. This requirement becomes even more essential with the development of smart buildings, emphasizing the necessity for precise and highly reliable load prediction. The viability and accuracy of machine learning models have shown promising outcomes in predicting medium-term loads. Mid-term load fore-casting (MTLF) is essential for optimizing the efficiency of smart building. By utilizing data mining and machine learning models, it is possible to effectively analyse historical data and extract valuable patterns and trends. However, MTLF is challenged by several uncertain factors and variables that affect the regular load consumption patterns. This paper undertakes a thorough comparative analysis of various machine learning modeling techniques for MTLF, utilizing one year of data collected from an actual commercial smart building. The primary objective is to evaluate the effectiveness of different machine learning load forecasting methods, including Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Regression and K-Nearest Neighbors models. To assess the models' performance coefficients such as Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) are utilized for evaluation. This study with medium-term load prediction includes linear and nonlinear parameters, such as temperature, humidity, and wind speed. By analysing the comparative study outcomes, a better understanding into the most effective forecasting model is achieved in favour of advancing energy demands and smart building technologies.

articleTitle: Analysis of Sub-Synchronous Oscillations in Grid-Connected Wind Farms and Hybrid PV/Battery Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: This paper presents methods to evaluate and analyze sub-synchronous oscillations (SSO) in wind energy systems utilizing doubly-fed induction generators (DFIG) and hybrid photovoltaic (PV)/battery energy storage systems (BESS) in series-compensated electrical networks. SSOs are evaluated on four test systems depicting the Induction Generator Effect(IGE), Sub-synchronous Torsional Interactions (SSTI), and Sub-Synchronous Resonance (SSR). Simulations conducted using PSCAD/EMTDC reveal how variations in series compensation, inertia constants, stator resistance, and Short Circuit Ratio (SCR) can cause SSO, impacting grid stability. Specifically, IGE is examined under different stator resistance values (0.01 pu and 0.015 pu), and torsional interactions are evaluated by adjusting inertia constants. Additionally, the study examines the role of integrated PV and BESS system controls in mitigating SSOs. The voltage harmonic injection method analyzes inverter harmonics across different dispatch levels, SCR levels, and power factors. A comparative analysis between traditional series capacitors and Thyristor-Controlled Series Reactors (TCSR) indicates that TCSR provides superior damping, reducing oscillatory amplitude in active and reactive power by up to 30 percentage points. With the increase in compensation levels, the resonant point shifts to the sub-synchronous region (20-40Hz). Moreover, inaccurately modeled active and reactive power controls can induce undamped oscillations in the sub-synchronous region depicted by a negative resistance in this region, affecting radially connected, series-compensated lines.

articleTitle: Who is Smart? Smart Metering and Billing System for Prosumer Microgrids With New-Type Multi-Source Energy Meters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel perspective on the concept of “smart” in the context of prosumer microgrids. Stan-dard “smart” solutions have primarily focused on the stability of energy production sources and transmission networks-that is, energy management systems can partially control the operation of consumer objects, deriving benefits such as balance and stability in the operation of the energy sources, transmission, and distribution lines. This paper presents a new-type, direct integration of the “smart” element on the consumers' side, allowing them to derive direct benefits from participating in a cluster that incorporates renewable energy sources, energy storage systems, and other energy-efficient sources that produce energy at a lower cost than that supplied by the grid. It has been achieved through the use of multi-source energy consumption meters, which make it possible to distinguish what portion of the energy flowing through the meter at any given time comes from the grid, what from renewable sources, or what from other sources present in the microgrid. This allows for the development of a more prosumer-oriented billing system. The described metering and billing system extends the concept of “smart” within prosumer microgrids, contributing to the further development of renewable energy-powered microgrids, with a particular emphasis on the benefits for prosumers.

articleTitle: Heuristic vs. Analytical Energy Hub Optimization: Design, Implementation, and Trade-Offs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Various algorithms can be used to optimize the operation of energy hubs, which differ in complexity and optimization quality. The heuristic Evolutionary Algorithm (EA) is able to approximate solutions to complex and non-convex problems. In comparison, the Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) and the Mixed-Integer Quadratic Program (MIQP) are able to compute the optimal solution of an approximated model. The present paper focuses on the comparison of energy hub schedule optimization using an EA, a MILP, and a MIQP. Furthermore, the source code for the MILP and MIQP models is publicly available. In our comparison, the analytical solver can optimize the schedule of an exemplary energy hub within seconds, and the EA takes multiple minutes to compute. The schedule generated with the analytical models follows the target closely with a similar root-mean-square error as the schedule generated by the EA.

articleTitle: Analysis of Current Density and Hydrogen Consumption in PEMFC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) can operate at low temperatures for rapid start-up. In this study, mathematical equations used for the single-cell PEMFC are solved for the counter flow arrangement. A three-dimensional, isothermal, and steady-state with a single-phase model is engaged to calculate the current flux density and the hydrogen consumption at different locations of the inlet of the fuel cell. The model solved the gas species distribution in a fuel cell. The acquired polarization curve is related to the reference model. Results indicated that for a high consumption of hydrogen, more current flux density is attained and for less consumption of hydrogen less current flux density is attained. When the temperature of the PEM fuel cell is increased by the electrochemical equations voltage increases so the current achieved decreases. The results indicate that at a temperature of 343K and at 0.7V, 0.8V and 0.9V mass fraction of hydrogen varies from 0.8 to 0.71, 0.8 to 0.734 and 0.8 to 0.773 respectively with respect to varying the distance of the inlet of the fuel cell to the outlet from 0 to 60 at a regular interval of 10mm.

articleTitle: Rotor Angle Stability Analysis with Coordinated Control of FACTS Devices Using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Electrical load demand on existing transmission lines is growing day by day throughout the world as the economy grows. This increase in electrical energy expenditure, as well as the growing introduction of non-linear loads into the power system, has compelled us to enhance power flow and stability. FACTS (Flexible AC Transmission System) is an important component of power system augmentation. Stability defines the stable operation of the system after abnormal conditions or contingencies to the power system. In this Paper, a particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is applied to design the coordinated parameters of static VAR compensator (SVC) and Thyristor Controlled Series Capacitor (TCSC). In this paper, standard 9-bus and 14-bus system has been considered for analysis of stability with inspecting disturbance at particular buses. The results obtained confirmed the proposed coordinated control technique for improvement of rotor angle and overall stability with reference to individual effects of FACTS device. The paper contributes operational concepts of FACTS and change in PSO algorithm to achieve coordinated control.

articleTitle: Optimization of Solar Energy System Integration for a Sustainable Healthcare Facility
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Amidst the electricity shortage and thus frequent power outages that Libya has been through, this study investigates integrating a solar photovoltaic (PV) energy system into an urban medical facility in Benghazi, namely Venice Dental Clinic (VDC). The research uses the PVsyst software to optimally utilize solar energy such that enhancing sustainability and save operational expenses. Two strategies pertaining solar-load delivery have been assessed; they are: full load and partial load mechanisms. The research methodology includes a comprehensive site investigation, data collection and simulation modeling. Two solar PV system designs were built and optimized, followed by a comparative analysis to analyze performance and efficiency. The results of the study showed that the two proposed load satisfaction methods significantly improve the energy efficiency of the clinic. The available roof space is also sufficient to install solar panels, demonstrating the feasibility and potential benefits of integrating solar energy into the healthcare sector. The optimized PV system is capable of covering up to 85% of the clinic's energy needs, resulting in an annual energy production of 30 MWh. This integration yields a significant reduction in electricity cost by 40%, thus enhancing the economic viability of the clinic. In addition, the installation has a positive impact towards eliminating carbon footprint. Above all, the project could serve as a showcase investment that can be successfully emulated by other private and public enterprises.

articleTitle: Revenue and Reliability Protection for Energy Suppliers From Energy Theft
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Energy theft poses technical and social challenges for utilities and legitimate customers. In recent years, numerous machine learning (ML) concepts have been used to enhance power system operations in support of energy sector transitions towards digitization. The objective of the work is to identify suitable approaches to counteract various energy theft methods. In this collaborative work we have applied ML models with the market demand trends to find the most suitable approach(es) for identifying energy stealing. The work begins with some relevant results using ensemble ML models for energy theft detection. We then introduce the Naive Bayes model, which has been used for handling classification problems through supervised learning. This model is used to develop a methodology for identifying energy theft based on customers' consumption patterns. Results were compared using false-positive and detection rates for assessing their effectiveness.

articleTitle: Optimal Smart Inverter Volt-Watt and Volt-Var Settings to Maximize Fair Contribution in Voltage Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Overvoltage resulting from the high penetration of photovoltaic (PV) sources in distribution networks is a major challenge. Approaches to mitigate such overvoltage conditions include curtailment of PV active power and the injection of reactive power by PV inverters. This paper proposes a centralized control strategy to optimize the Volt-Watt and Volt-Var profiles such that active and reactive power of all PV inverters are controlled to not only to mitigate against overvoltage conditions but to do so in a manner where curtailment of active power is equalized or balanced in a fairly manner across all inverters. The Imperialist Competitive Algorithm (ICA) algorithm is used to optimize the objective functions. MATLAB and Open DSS software are used to simulate the grid model and optimize goals.

articleTitle: Improving Decision-Making in Distribution Networks Using Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: In today's digital distribution grid, characterized by the abundance of data, the importance of data analytics cannot be overstated. It plays a crucial role in ensuring operational excellence by providing distribution operators with real-time insights and aiding system planning engineers in making well-informed business decisions. By harnessing both historical and real-time data from Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADMS), utilities are empowered to make data-driven decisions based on past trends, events, and forecasts. Through a data analytics lens, the study delves into four specific test cases: 1) conducting periodic reviews/sanity checks on protection settings within a specific area or zone, 2) effectively managing fault circuit indicators (CFCI) communication, 3) validating Feeder Health Index, and 4) assessing the impact of new technologies deployed as pilots. These case studies serve to showcase how leveraging data analytics can optimize decision-making processes within modern distribution systems. They highlight the ability of data analytics to offer valuable insights into system performance, preempt potential issues, and streamline resource allocation. Furthermore, the study emphasizes how data analytics can enhance reliability and efficiency by enabling predictive maintenance and improving grid operations. Ultimately, the case studies underscore the transformative influence of data analytics on decision-making within contemporary distribution systems, setting the stage for more efficient and sustainable energy management practices.

articleTitle: Evaluate the Effectiveness of Intelligent Control Approaches in Building Energy Performance - A Hybrid Energy Resource Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: This paper aims to develop multi-objective controllers to improve the environmental footprints of hybrid energy resources buildings. Accordingly, a multi-source heating system is implemented to evaluate the potential of three kinds of controllers. We use a case study analysis of an apartment to study building system components: boiler, solar thermal panel, storage tank, and electrical heater. Three kinds of controllers are analyzed: a) a combination of Model Predictive Controller (MPC) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) (MP-GA), b) an optimized fuzzy sliding mode controller, and c) a traditional on/off controller. The controllers optimize the heating system by regulating the supplied energy from each energy resource. Our findings indicate that the fuzzy sliding mode controller and MPC-GA provided comfortable temperature levels 99% and 97% of the time, respectively. Furthermore, they improved heating energy savings by up to 9% compared to the on/off baseline, primarily due to their ability to estimate the supplied energy from the solar thermal panel and storage system.

articleTitle: A Genetic Algorithm and Graph Theory Based Restoration Mechanism for Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: With the proliferating demand for stability, reliability and QoS in modern large-scale distribution systems, an efficient automated supply restoration mechanism has become a significant concern. The reliability of any distribution system trust upon it's resilience to attacks and post-fault restoration mechanism. Fault restoration on power grids is a multi-constrained complex optimization problem and is mostly carried out with the help of tie lines and sectionalizing switches. This work proposes a two-phase novel and scalable mechanism based on Genetic Algorithm and graph theory approach to restore a radial distribution network under attack, by imposters or due to natural calamities. The first phase is achieved by identifying a configuration that optimizes the power losses, followed by a second phase that minimizes the load shed without compromising the physical, topological and operational constraints. The experiment is carried out while considering the three key phenomena like optimal topology, optimum required switch operations and the time consumed to achieve restored configuration to minimize the load being shed. The performance of the proposed approach is compared against the state-of-the-art techniques for different cases of faults on IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 417-bus systems. Fitness evolution graphs show that experiments yielded encouraging results.

articleTitle: Digital Forensics: A Survey of Emerging Threats, Challenges, and Opportunities in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: The era of digital technology has been introduced into the environment of the smart grid, which in turn increases its vulnerability to cyber threats due to the interconnected and cyber physical nature. These potential cyberthreats may interrupt the process of energy distribution, which may also jeopardize the essential grid infrastructure, causing enormous damage. The existing digital forensic frameworks are not equipped to address digital forensic issues within the complex smart grid environment. In this work, we present an assessment of the limitations of the existing digital forensic frameworks and technologies over smart grid settings. The main emphasis of this article is to analyze the unique issues in the smart grid network by conducting a systematic review of the literature. In addition, some of the real-life case studies have been discussed in the quest to demonstrate how other frameworks have been exploited to address these pressing challenges.

articleTitle: Addressing Explainability in Load Forecasting Using Time Series Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Energy management is a crucial issue in the modern world, as it affects various aspects of human life and the environment. It is a complex and challenging task that involves multiple factors and uncertainties. Machine learning has been widely adopted for improving building energy efficiency and flexibility in the past decade, as it can leverage the massive building operational data to provide accurate and reliable predictions and recommendations. However, with the increasing complexity, machine learning models are becoming black-boxes that are difficult to understand and trust by end-users. Hence, Explainable AI (XAI) has gained significant popularity in last years. In this paper, we focus on the explainability of different machine learning methods with regards to electricity consumption prediction. We apply explainability methods to interpret the results of these models and to provide insights into the factors that affect the electricity consumption. We use the Grenoble University building dataset, a non-aggregated dataset that contains electricity consumption data for different types of rooms over a period of two years. We evaluate the performance and the interpretability of the machine learning models and we discuss the implications and the limitations of our approach.

articleTitle: Solar Energy Forecasting Using Statistical, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Solar energy is one of the vital Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) for creating a Virtual Power Plant (VPP). However, its integration into the electricity grid is challenged by its intermittent nature due to fluctuating weather conditions. Thus, Solar energy forecasting is crucial to ensure a stable and reliable power supply. This paper performs solar energy forecasting using statistical, machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) approaches. A comprehensive analysis of existing literature reveals a gap in comparative studies and real-world implementation considerations. In this paper, these problems are addressed by providing a system design and modeling framework that incorporates real-world challenges such as data delays, feature selection adaptability, etc. Solar power generation was forecasted 3 hours ahead and the performance of different algorithms was evaluated including investigating the underlying reasons for their effectiveness. Results indicate that machine learning models, particularly Random Forest, outperform others with the lowest RMSE and MAE, while statistical models exhibit the least accuracy. The study was concluded with recommendations for practical implementation and directions for future research.

articleTitle: Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning for Balancing Energy Efficiency and Occupant Comfort
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Using Reinforcement Learning (RL) to control the energy consumption while preserving the comfort level in a building has shown promising. For instance, in our previous work, we have proposed a first implementation of RL, where we have defined the energy use environment by a minimal set of parameters representing the indoor temperature, humidity and the light intensity. Although, this first implementation has shown good results, the set of states, actions and the reward function are over simplified and can be fairly improved to better represent a reel occupant behavior including energy operation and human comfort. In this paper, we extend our RL customization by defining a new state representation, new actions and new reward function that considers more descriptive indoor building features and a more elaborated comfort that considers thermal, and visual comforts and the indoor air quality. Due to the increased complexity brought by the new state space, a new variant of Deep RL is used to allow appropriate decision making when choosing action for efficient energy consumption while maintaining occupant comfort. The proposed RL customization is used to control a realistic simulated energy-use environment developed using EnergyPlus and OpenStudio. Using different scenarios of using energy with a building, the results show that our DRL was able to learn a policy that controls the simulated environment. The DRL leads to an energy saving ranging from 5% to 17% while maintaining a same comfort when compared with the thermostat Strategy.

articleTitle: A Method for Determining the Topology of Multiple Low-Voltage Radial Distribution Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: As renewable energy is integrated into power grids on a large scale, grid operations have higher safety and efficiency requirements. Smart meters, providing real-time data of grid nodes every 15min, enable grid operators to monitor and preemptively address potential issues. However, a large part of the topology of low-voltage distribution grids remains unobservable due to limited communication links in switch devices at the low-voltage level. This paper proposes a novel method to reconstruct the topology of multiple low-voltage radial distribution grids using voltage data measured by smart meters. Employing minimum spanning tree, the method identifies interconnecting topologies of multiple low-voltage radial distribution grids and partitions them through unsupervised learning algorithms to exclude anomalous connections. Validation on a benchmark dataset confirms the method's efficacy, demonstrating intactness in separating and accurately reconstructing the topology of modeled low-voltage radial distribution grids.

articleTitle: Application of Deep Learning and Neural Networks for Smart Grid Stability Predictions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Efficient and sustainable electrical grids are crucial for energy management in modern society and industry. Govern-ments recognize this and prioritize energy management in their plans, alongside significant progress made in theory and practice over the years. The complexity of power systems determines the unique nature of power communication networks, and most researches have been focusing on the dynamic nature of voltage stability, which led to the need for dynamic models of power systems. Control strategies based on stability assessments have become essential for managing grid stability, diverging from traditional methods and often leveraging advanced computational techniques based on deep learning algorithms and neural networks. This way, researchers can develop predictive models capable of forecasting voltage stability and detecting potential instability events in real-time, whereas neural networks can also optimize control strategies based on wide-area information and grid response, enabling more effective stability control measures, as well as detecting and classifying disturbances or faults in the grid. This paper explores the use of predictive models to assess smart grid stability, examining the benefits, risks, and comparing results to determine the most effective approach.

articleTitle: Towards a Simplified and Integrated Model for Climate-Energy Resources and Systems Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: This study examines sustainable energy development (SED) and climate change (CC). An existing critical discourse analysis of the relationship between SED and CC found ten interconnected SED themes, two of which are energy financing and the demand for 100% renewable energy (RE), which have been least studied in SED literature but are useful in addressing the current progress of the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) aimed at reducing the global climate change consequences. Three environmental, economic, and energy models are introduced to examine the limits of current Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) to the 1.5 °C climate scenario using a just transition strategy for GHG emissions reduction. The environment (ENV) model estimates global temperature rises using baseline, current (announced energy policies 1 and 2), optimal (2.0 °C Scenario), and most optimal (1.5 °C Scenario) climatic scenarios. The study analyses predicted temperature rises for each climate policy scenario to construct a simpler integrated emissions cost budgeting strategy using capital budgeting approaches under the economic (ECO) model to evaluate the four scenarios' economic attractiveness. The Energy (ENE) model synthesises 100% renewable energy (RE) possibilities in the four heavily driven CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission sectors (electricity, transport, building, and industrial processes) to demonstrate the essential idea of the possibility of a global 100% RE system. The feasibility of 100% RE and global temperature rise under four scenarios is assessed using system dynamics-based integrated evaluation. The study illuminates SED's challenges, opportunities, and paths to planning a more sustainable energy future. It also shows how climate change scenarios could influence policy toward planning for sustainable energy resources and climate resilience systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Two Novel Supervised Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Non-intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) is a critical tool in energy management which allows disaggregating total electricity consumption into individual appliance-level energy consumption within a household or commercial setting, all without the need for intrusive monitoring devices. NILM empowers consumers, utilities, and researchers to gain a deeper understanding of how electricity is utilized, aiding in energy conservation, billing, and load optimization. This paper introduces two pioneering supervised NILM models designed to enhance load disaggregation accuracy and versatility in both tertiary and residential environment. The first model presented in this research is a machine learning model which employs a unique fusion of Bayesian optimization technique over ensemble learning approach. The Machine Learning based ensemble approach leverages the complementary strength of six different regressor techniques and the Bayesian optimization technique optimizes various parameters of the regressors. Thus, this proposed machine learning model effectively enhances the NILM system's adaptability to various electrical environments and scenarios. The second model adopts a Deep Learning technique based on Temporal Convolutional Network architecture for NILM regression task by efficiently capturing temporal dependencies of the sequential NILM data. The models were evaluated based on two energy consumption data collected from a tertiary (university laboratory) and a residential setting. The preliminary results of the novel approaches indicate substantial improvements in load disaggregation accuracy when compared to recent benchmarking NILM techniques.

articleTitle: Critical Materials for Electric Vehicles in Sub-Sahara Africa: Opportunities and Preparedness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: In the wake of the global shift towards electric vehicles (EVs), sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) faces both possibilities and threats. Although this region has large quantities of critical materials (CMs) needed for electric vehicle batteries and fuel cells, it is not yet ready to host the EV material supply chain. The study presents an overview of the role of CM in EV development and evaluates SSA current EV supply chain, with emphasis on policies and technologies supporting the CM utilization. It looks at the success of the policies put in place by some SSA countries to encourage the adoption of electric vehicles through the development of critical materials potentials. As these critical materials are instrumental to the manufacturing of batteries for BEV and fuel cells for the FCEV, hence, this study offers an overview of CM in SSA with some three vital suggestions. The three suggestions include keys policy brief to support project development to host the EV CM market, managing the unevenness in CM distribution, and strategic partnership to catalyse the development of a robust centralised policy and regulatory instrument. With the full adoption and implementation of these suggestions, SSA countries would be fully equipped to embrace the EV revolution and take advantage of its environmental, social, and economic benefits.

articleTitle: Physics-Informed NN for Improving Electric Vehicles Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Charge Estimation Robustness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are often powered by lithium-ion batteries. To ensure the reliability of EVs, it is essential to model and predict the remaining useful life of these batteries. Accurate estimation of the state of charge (SoC) is a critical aspect for effectively managing and ensuring operational reliability of battery systems. Building principled accurate models is challenging due to the complex electrochemistry that governs battery operation. This research paper presents a novel approach that utilizes Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to enhance the accuracy of SoC estimation. PINNs combine the data-driven learning capabilities of neural networks with the fundamental physical laws that govern battery dynamics. By incorporating both aspects, PINNs offer a novel way to improve the accuracy of SoC estimation in lithium-ion batteries and enable better management of battery systems in the context of electric vehicles. We demonstrate how incorporating physical constraints into the learning process enhances model prediction performance and ensures physically plausible solutions. The approach is validated using data publicly available through the Mendeley Data website by McMaster University in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. Results showed that our proposed robust approach can successfully overcome the measurement's errors and noise. Moreover, the model can obtain an SoC estimation accuracy of less than 2.85% root mean squared error (RMSE).

articleTitle: Review on Virtual Power Plant for Hierarchical Control Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: As more distributed energy resources (DERs) are integrated into the power system, there is a growing need to manage them effectively. Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) have emerged to address this need by aggregating diverse energy resources such as photovoltaic systems (PVs), Wind turbines, energy storage systems (ESS), and electric vehicles (EVs). VPPs help balance the grid supply and demand, sell excess power, enhance system reliability, supporting renewable energy and improving overall efficiency. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of VPP technologies, focusing on control methods and energy management applications. The paper presents an overview of the core components of VPPs along with the global market growth forecasts for DERs until 2030 and discusses the importance of hierarchical control for ancillary services, including recent contributions at the primary, secondary, and tertiary control techniques. Additionally, the paper examines five real-world VPP projects in North America and identifies exploring future research directions and opportunities in VPP, emphasizing the need for ongoing innovation to address new challenges and optimize renewable energy integration into the grid.

articleTitle: Advancing Africa's Sustainable Energy Development Through Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) as Low-Carbon Power Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 12th International Conference on Smart Energy Grid Engineering (SEGE)
abstract: Access to affordable, reliable, and clean energy is vital for achieving the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals. In Africa, where about 79% of electricity comes from fossil fuels, transitioning to low-carbon systems is crucial to limit global warming and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. However, the reliance on intermittent renewables, like solar and wind poses challenges due to their variable supply. This paper explores the role of small modular reactors (SMRs) in advancing sustainable energy development in Africa. SMRs are advanced nuclear reactors with capacities of up to 300 MW(e) per unit, offering a promising alternative to fossil fuel gensets, particularly for underserved communities. The paper examines key issues in Africa's energy sector and highlights SMRs as a viable solution. The paper reveals that SMRs, with their modular design, efficiency, flexibility, safety features, and extended fuel cycles, can bridge the energy gap in remote and rural African communities. Thus, integrating SMRs with existing grids or operating off-grid, can provide electricity to those currently lacking basic services. Combining SMRs with solar and wind energy systems could enhance universal energy access, thereby, supporting the ambitious sustainable energy future. Therefore, advancing Africa's sustainable energy development through SMRs is essential for achieving low-carbon power generation.
